title: Pocket Skill metadata
description: Pocket-specific metadata for an Agent Skill, stored as pocket.json alongside SKILL.md. SKILL.md itself follows the open Agent Skills format (agentskills.io) and carries only `name` and `description` in its frontmatter — everything Pocket-specific lives here instead, so the skill stays valid for other runtimes.

$schema.description: This schema's URL. Enables validation and editor autocomplete.

category.description: Which marketplace filter this skill appears under. One of a fixed set, so a skill cannot invent a category that no filter shows.

author.description: The publisher's GitHub handle. Combined with the skill name it forms the skill's unique reference, @author/name — a bare name is NOT unique, since unrelated publishers commonly ship skills with the same one.

roles.description: Agent roles this skill suits. Empty or absent means any role. Used to suggest a skill to the right agent rather than to restrict installation.

license.description: SPDX identifier, or a short phrase if the licence is not an SPDX one.

homepage.description: Where to read more about this skill.

keywords.description: Extra search terms. The description is already indexed, so use this only for words a reader would search but the description would not naturally contain.

requiresConnectors.description: Connectors this skill assumes are available. A skill teaches an agent HOW to do something; if it also needs the ABILITY, name the connectors here so the marketplace can warn about a skill that cannot act.

adaptedFrom.description: Provenance, when this skill is derived from one published elsewhere. Recording it is required by most upstream licences and is shown in the marketplace, so credit is visible rather than implied.

note.description: What was changed in adapting it. Worth stating plainly — a reader comparing the two should not have to diff them.

deprecated.description: Set when a skill should no longer be installed. The string is shown to anyone who has it installed, so say what to use instead.
